correctness.rationale: For perfect graphs, the verified H-description consists exactly of coordinate nonnegativity and maximal-clique inequalities. A radius-r ball centered at c therefore satisfies c_v>=r and c(C)+r sqrt(|C|)<=1. A maximum clique combines these into r(omega+sqrt(omega))<=1; the uniform center attains equality because k+sqrt(k) is increasing. These same inequalities give the complete incenter locus. Equality on maximum cliques proves the maximum-clique-cover uniqueness criterion, and strict slack at any uncovered vertex proves the converse. The facet and tangency claims are separately justified.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a direct Euclidean interpretation of the clique number, and hence of the chromatic number throughout the perfect-graph class. It also turns the combinatorial property 'maximum cliques cover all vertices' into an exact geometric uniqueness criterion for the Chebyshev center, and identifies the complete active facet structure of the canonical maximal ball. This is a natural family-wide structural metric statement about a central polytope in perfect-graph theory, not a finite table, arbitrary slice, or mere renaming.
